title: Longest Line, Streaming
prompt: Implement longest_line(path) returning the longest line (stripped of the trailing newline) of a text file WITHOUT loading the whole file — iterate lazily. Empty file returns ''.

tests.name: finds the longest
tests.code:
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile
p = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / 'log.txt'
p.write_text('short' + chr(10) + 'a much longer line here' + chr(10) + 'mid', encoding='utf-8')
assert longest_line(p) == 'a much longer line here'
tests.hint: Track the max while iterating the file object directly.

tests.name: empty file
tests.code:
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile
p = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / 'empty.txt'
p.write_text('', encoding='utf-8')
assert longest_line(p) == ''

tests.name: streams instead of slurping
tests.code:
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile
p = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / 'big.txt'
p.write_text(chr(10).join(['l' * i for i in range(1, 2000)]), encoding='utf-8')
def _no_slurp(self, *a, **k):
    raise AssertionError('read_text() slurps the whole file - stream line by line instead')
Path.read_text = _no_slurp
assert longest_line(p) == 'l' * 1999
tests.hint: Track the longest line as you read; never load the whole file at once.
